sanskrit: evam asmi tadā muktaḥ kathaṃ cit tena saṃyuge idānīm api yad vṛttaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva yad uttaram
english: In this way I was barely freed from him in that combat. Now hear what further occurred even after that.

sanskrit: rākṣasābhyām ahaṃ dvābhyām anirviṇṇas tathā kṛtaḥ sahito mṛgarūpābhyāṃ praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
english: Undeterred even after being so dealt with by those two rākṣasas, I entered the Daṇḍaka forest together with them, both of them having taken the form of deer.

sanskrit: dīptajihvo mahākāyas tīkṣṇaśṛṇgo mahābalaḥ vyacaran daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ māṃsabhakṣo mahāmṛgaḥ
english: With blazing tongue, a great body, sharp horns, and immense strength, I roamed the Daṇḍaka forest as a mighty beast, feeding on flesh.

sanskrit: agnihotreṣu tīrtheṣu caityavṛkṣeṣu rāvaṇa atyantaghoro vyacaraṃs tāpasāṃs tān pradharṣayan
english: O Rāvaṇa, utterly terrible, I roamed about at sacrificial fires, at sacred fords, at holy trees — harassing the ascetics there.

sanskrit: nihatya daṇḍakāraṇye tāpasān dharmacāriṇaḥ rudhirāṇi pibaṃs teṣāṃ tathā māṃsāni bhakṣayan
english: Slaying the pious ascetics in the Daṇḍaka forest, I drank their blood and devoured their flesh.

sanskrit: ṛṣimāṃsāśanaḥ krūras trāsayan vanagocarān tadā rudhiramatto 'haṃ vyacaraṃ daṇḍakāvanam
english: Eating the flesh of sages, cruel and intoxicated with blood, I wandered through the Daṇḍaka forest, terrifying all who dwelt there.

sanskrit: tadāhaṃ daṇḍakāraṇye vicaran dharmadūṣakaḥ āsādayaṃ tadā rāmaṃ tāpasaṃ dharmam āśritam
english: While I was thus ranging through the Daṇḍaka forest as a transgressor of righteousness, I then encountered Rāma — an ascetic abiding in dharma.

sanskrit: vaidehīṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham tāpasaṃ niyatāhāraṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam
english: And the illustrious Vaidehī, and Lakṣmaṇa the great warrior — an ascetic of regulated diet, devoted to the welfare of all creatures.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ vanagataṃ rāmaṃ paribhūya mahābalam tāpaso 'yam iti jñātvā pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: I — recalling old enmity and thinking him merely an ascetic — showed contempt for the mighty Rāma dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: abhyadhāvaṃ susaṃkruddhas tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo mṛgākṛtiḥ jighāṃsur akṛtaprajñas taṃ prahāram anusmaran
english: In a form of a deer with sharp horns, full of rage, mindless, remembering his previous blow against me, I rushed at him with intent to kill.

sanskrit: tena muktās trayo bāṇāḥ śitāḥ śatrunibarhaṇāḥ vikṛṣya balavac cāpaṃ suparṇānilatulyagāḥ
english: He drew his great bow with force and released three sharp arrows, destroyers of enemies, swift as Garuḍa or the wind.

sanskrit: te bāṇā vajrasaṃkāśāḥ sughorā raktabhojanāḥ ājagmuḥ sahitāḥ sarve trayaḥ saṃnataparvaṇaḥ
english: Those three arrows, thunderbolt-like, utterly terrible, feeding on blood, and straight-jointed, came flying together and struck.

sanskrit: parākramajño rāmasya śaṭho dṛṣṭabhayaḥ purā samutkrāntas tato muktas tāv ubhau rākṣasau hatau
english: I, the cheat, knowing Rāma's prowess and having felt his power before, sprang up and fled — and both those rākṣasas were slain.

sanskrit: śareṇa mukto rāmasya kathaṃ cit prāpya jīvitam iha pravrājito yuktas tāpaso 'haṃ samāhitaḥ
english: Barely escaping Rāma's arrow alive, I was banished here, and now I live as a composed ascetic, disciplined and intent.

sanskrit: vṛkṣe vṛkṣe hi paśyāmi cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaram gṛhītadhanuṣaṃ rāmaṃ pāśahastam ivāntakam
english: In every tree I see Rāma wearing bark-cloth and black antelope skin, bearing his bow, like Death himself with a noose in hand.

sanskrit: api rāmasahasrāṇi bhītaḥ paśyāmi rāvaṇa rāmabhūtam idaṃ sarvam araṇyaṃ pratibhāti me
english: In my fear I see thousands of Rāmas, O Rāvaṇa — this entire forest appears to me as if it were Rāma himself.

sanskrit: rāmam eva hi paśyāmi rahite rākṣaseśvara dṛṣṭvā svapnagataṃ rāmam udbhramāmi vicetanaḥ
english: Even in solitude, O lord of rākṣasas, I see only Rāma — seeing Rāma even in my dreams, I start up senseless.

sanskrit: rakārādīni nāmāni rāmatrastasya rāvaṇa ratnāni ca rathāś caiva trāsaṃ saṃjanayanti me
english: O Rāvaṇa, every name beginning with the syllable 'ra' — and even jewels and chariots — causes terror in me, so frightened am I of Rāma.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tasya prabhāvajño na yuddhaṃ tena te kṣamam raṇe rāmeṇa yudhyasva kṣamāṃ vā kuru rākṣasa na te rāmakathā kāryā yadi māṃ draṣṭum icchasi
english: I know his power well — battle with him is not fitting for you. Either fight Rāma in battle, or make peace, O rākṣasa. If you wish to see me again, speak no further of Rāma.

sanskrit: idaṃ vaco bandhuhitārthinā mayā yathocyamānaṃ yadi nābhipatsyase sabāndhavas tyakṣyasi jīvitaṃ raṇe hato 'dya rāmeṇa śarair ajihmagaiḥ
english: This counsel, spoken by me for the good of your kinsmen — if you do not heed it as spoken, you and your kinsmen shall lose your lives, slain today in battle by Rāma's straight-flying arrows.

sanskrit: mārīcena tu tad vākyaṃ kṣamaṃ yuktaṃ ca rāvaṇaḥ ukto na pratijagrāha martukāma ivauṣadham
english: Rāvaṇa, thus addressed by Mārīca with words appropriate and fitting, did not accept them — as one who desires death refuses medicine.

sanskrit: taṃ pathyahitavaktāraṃ mārīcaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyam ayuktaṃ kālacoditaḥ
english: The lord of rākṣasas, driven by fate, spoke harsh and unsuitable words to Mārīca, who had spoken what was wholesome and beneficial.

sanskrit: yat kilaitad ayuktārthaṃ mārīca mayi kathyate vākyaṃ niṣphalam atyarthaṃ bījam uptam ivoṣare
english: "What is told to me by you, O Mārīca, is altogether improper in meaning — utterly fruitless speech, like seed sown in barren ground.

sanskrit: tvadvākyair na tu māṃ śakyaṃ bhettuṃ rāmasya saṃyuge pāpaśīlasya mūrkhasya mānuṣasya viśeṣataḥ
english: By your words you cannot shake my resolve in battle against Rāma — especially not against that sinful, foolish mortal.

sanskrit: yas tyaktvā suhṛdo rājyaṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tathā strīvākyaṃ prākṛtaṃ śrutvā vanam ekapade gataḥ
english: He who abandoned friends, kingdom, mother, and father alike — and at the ordinary words of a woman departed to the forest at one step.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā tasya saṃyuge kharaghātinaḥ prāṇaiḥ priyatarā sītā hartavyā tava saṃnidhau
english: Sītā, more dear to him than life, must certainly be taken from that slayer of Khara in combat — before your very eyes.

sanskrit: evaṃ me niścitā buddhir hṛdi mārīca vartate na vyāvartayituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: Such, O Mārīca, is the firm resolve that abides in my heart — it cannot be turned back even by the gods and asuras with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: doṣaṃ guṇaṃ vā saṃpṛṣṭas tvam evaṃ vaktum arhasi apāyaṃ vāpy upāyaṃ vā kāryasyāsya viniścaye
english: When asked, you ought to speak of fault or virtue, of risk or remedy — in determining what is to be done in this matter.

sanskrit: saṃpṛṣṭena tu vaktavyaṃ sacivena vipaścitā udyatāñjalinā rājño ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: A wise minister who desires his own welfare, when questioned, should speak to the king with hands raised in reverence.

sanskrit: vākyam apratikūlaṃ tu mṛdupūrvaṃ śubhaṃ hitam upacāreṇa yuktaṃ ca vaktavyo vasudhādhipaḥ
english: The lord of the earth should be addressed with speech that is not contrary, beginning with gentleness, auspicious, beneficial, and delivered with proper courtesy.

sanskrit: sāvamardaṃ tu yad vākyaṃ mārīca hitam ucyate nābhinandati tad rājā mānārho mānavarjitam
english: But the beneficial counsel that is spoken condescendingly, O Mārīca — a king worthy of honour does not rejoice in such words, stripped as they are of respect.

sanskrit: pañcarūpāṇi rājāno dhārayanty amitaujasaḥ agner indrasya somasya yamasya varuṇasya ca auṣṇyaṃ tathā vikramaṃ ca saumyaṃ daṇḍaṃ prasannatām
english: Kings of immeasurable might bear five natures: those of Agni, Indra, Soma, Yama, and Varuṇa — heat and valour, graciousness, punishment, and serenity.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu mānyāḥ pūjyāś ca pārthivāḥ tvaṃ tu dharmam avijñāya kevalaṃ moham āsthitaḥ
english: Therefore kings are to be honoured and revered in all circumstances. But you, not understanding dharma, have resorted to mere delusion.

sanskrit: abhyāgataṃ māṃ daurātmyāt paruṣaṃ vadasīdṛśam guṇadoṣau na pṛcchāmi kṣamaṃ cātmani rākṣasa asmiṃs tu sa bhavān kṛtye sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhati
english: You address me, your guest, with such harsh words out of malice. I do not question merits and faults, nor what is appropriate for myself, O rākṣasa — in this matter, you ought to render me assistance.

sanskrit: sauvarṇas tvaṃ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ pralobhayitvā vaidehīṃ yatheṣṭaṃ gantum arhasi
english: Becoming a golden deer, dappled with silver spots, you shall entice Vaidehī and then go where you please.

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu māyāmṛgaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāñcanaṃ jātavismayā ānayainam iti kṣipraṃ rāmaṃ vakṣyati maithilī
english: Seeing you, a magical golden deer, Maithilī — full of wonder — will quickly say to Rāma: 'Bring me this creature.'

sanskrit: apakrānte ca kākutsthe lakṣmaṇe ca yathāsukham ānayiṣyāmi vaidehīṃ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīm iva
english: And when Kākutstha has gone away, and Lakṣmaṇa too, I shall carry off Vaidehī at ease, just as the thousand-eyed Indra carried off Śacī.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā tv idaṃ kāryaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha rākṣasa rājyasyārdhaṃ pradāsyāmi mārīca tava suvrata
english: Having accomplished this task, go where you please, O rākṣasa. I shall give you half the kingdom, O Mārīca of good vows."

sanskrit: gaccha saumya śivaṃ mārgaṃ kāryasyāsya vivṛddhaye prāpya sītām ayuddhena vañcayitvā tu rāghavam laṅkāṃ prati gamiṣyāmi kṛtakāryaḥ saha tvayā
english: "Go, dear one, travel a safe path for the accomplishment of this task. Having obtained Sītā and deceived Rāghava without battle, I shall return to Laṅkā with you, my purpose fulfilled."

sanskrit: etat kāryam avaśyaṃ me balād api kariṣyasi rājño hi pratikūlastho na jātu sukham edhate
english: "You shall carry out this task for me, even by compulsion — for one who opposes a king never prospers in any way."

sanskrit: āsādya taṃ jīvitasaṃśayas te mṛtyur dhruvo hy adya mayā virudhya etad yathāvat parigṛhya buddhyā yad atra pathyaṃ kuru tat tathā tvam
english: "Should you encounter him, your life will be in peril — death is certain if you oppose me today. Having considered this properly with your mind, do that which is best for you here."

sanskrit: ājñapto rājavad vākyaṃ pratikūlaṃ niśācaraḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ mārīco rākṣasādhipam
english: Thus commanded, the night-wanderer Mārīca, though the order was contrary to his counsel, spoke harsh words to the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: kenāyam upadiṣṭas te vināśaḥ pāpakarmaṇā saputrasya sarāṣṭrasya sāmātyasya niśācara
english: "By what evil-doer has this destruction been counselled to you, O night-wanderer — destruction of you with your sons, your kingdom, and your ministers?

sanskrit: kas tvayā sukhinā rājan nābhinandati pāpakṛt kenedam upadiṣṭaṃ te mṛtyudvāram upāyataḥ
english: "What sinful one, O king, does not rejoice in your happiness? By whom has this gateway to death been pointed out to you as a course of action?

sanskrit: śatravas tava suvyaktaṃ hīnavīryā niśācara icchanti tvāṃ vinaśyantam uparuddhaṃ balīyasā
english: "Clearly your enemies, O night-wanderer — weak in valour — desire to see you destroyed, restrained by one mightier than yourself.

sanskrit: kenedam upadiṣṭaṃ te kṣudreṇāhitavādinā yas tvām icchati naśyantaṃ svakṛtena niśācara
english: "By what base and malicious counsellor has this been advised to you — one who desires to see you perish by your own deed, O night-wanderer?

sanskrit: vadhyāḥ khalu na hanyante sacivās tava rāvaṇa ye tvām utpatham ārūḍhaṃ na nigṛhṇanti sarvaśaḥ
english: "Your ministers, O Rāvaṇa, deserve death and yet are not slain — those who do not restrain you in every way when you have strayed onto a wrong path.

sanskrit: amātyaiḥ kāmavṛtto hi rājā kāpatham āśritaḥ nigrāhyaḥ sarvathā sadbhir na nigrāhyo nigṛhyase
english: "Indeed, a king swayed by passion who has taken a wicked path must be restrained in every way by virtuous men — yet you, who ought to be restrained, are not being restrained.

sanskrit: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca yaśaś ca jayatāṃ vara svāmiprasādāt sacivāḥ prāpnuvanti niśācara
english: "Dharma, wealth, pleasure, and glory — ministers attain all these through the favour of their lord, O best of conquerors, O night-wanderer.

sanskrit: viparyaye tu tat sarvaṃ vyarthaṃ bhavati rāvaṇa vyasanaṃ svāmivaiguṇyāt prāpnuvantītare janāḥ
english: "But in the reverse case, all that becomes worthless, O Rāvaṇa — and other people too suffer calamity on account of a flawed master.

sanskrit: rājamūlo hi dharmaś ca jayaś ca jayatāṃ vara tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu rakṣitavyo narādhipaḥ
english: "For dharma and victory both have the king as their root, O best of conquerors. Therefore the lord of men must be protected in all circumstances.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ pālayituṃ śakyaṃ na tīkṣṇena niśācara na cāpi pratikūlena nāvinītena rākṣasa
english: "A kingdom cannot be governed by one who is harsh, O night-wanderer, nor by one who is contrary, nor by one who is ill-bred, O rākṣasa.

sanskrit: ye tīkṣṇamantrāḥ sacivā bhajyante saha tena vai viṣameṣu rathāḥ śīghraṃ mandasārathayo yathā
english: "Ministers who give harsh counsel are broken along with their king in adversity — just as swift chariots with poor drivers come to ruin on rough terrain.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ sādhavo loke yuktadharmam anuṣṭhitāḥ pareṣām aparādhena vinaṣṭāḥ saparicchadāḥ
english: "Many virtuous men in the world, who practised dharma fittingly, have been ruined together with their households because of the transgressions of others.

sanskrit: svāminā pratikūlena prajās tīkṣṇena rāvaṇa rakṣyamāṇā na vardhante meṣā gomāyunā yathā
english: "Subjects guarded by a harsh and perverse master do not flourish, O Rāvaṇa — just as sheep do not thrive when guarded by a jackal.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ vinaśiṣyanti sarve rāvaṇa rākṣasāḥ yeṣāṃ tvaṃ karkaśo rājā durbuddhir ajitendriyaḥ
english: "All the rākṣasas will surely perish, O Rāvaṇa — those whose king you are: harsh, evil-minded, with unmastered senses.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ kākatālīyaṃ ghoram āsāditaṃ tvayā atra kiṃ śobhanaṃ yat tvaṃ sasainyo vinaśiṣyasi
english: "You have brought about this terrible crow-and-palm coincidence upon yourself. What is auspicious in this — that you shall perish together with your army?

sanskrit: māṃ nihatya tu rāmo 'sau nacirāt tvāṃ vadhiṣyati anena kṛtakṛtyo 'smi mriye yad ariṇā hataḥ
english: "After killing me, that Rāma will swiftly slay you as well. By this I consider my purpose fulfilled — that I die slain by an enemy.

sanskrit: darśanād eva rāmasya hataṃ mām upadhāraya ātmānaṃ ca hataṃ viddhi hṛtvā sītāṃ sabāndhavam
english: "At the very sight of Rāma, consider me already slain. And know yourself slain too, along with all your kinsmen, once you have abducted Sītā.

sanskrit: ānayiṣyasi cet sītām āśramāt sahito mayā naiva tvam asi naivāhaṃ naiva laṅkā na rākṣasāḥ
english: "If you bring Sītā from her hermitage, with me as your accomplice — neither you shall exist, nor I, nor Laṅkā, nor the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: nivāryamāṇas tu mayā hitaiṣiṇā na mṛṣyase vākyam idaṃ niśācara paretakalpā hi gatāyuṣo narā hitaṃ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhir īritam
english: "Though restrained by me who wish you well, you do not endure this counsel, O night-wanderer — for men whose lives are spent, resembling the dead, do not accept the benefit spoken by friends."
